1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, wherein the non-native compartment is __not naturally occurring in the cell__.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo __from heterologous nucleic acid encoding the at least one BMC polypeptide__.

3. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme __that is not naturally associated with the BMC polypeptide in the cell__.

4. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes __that catalyze sequential enzymatic reactions__.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 or claim 4 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence __that directs the enzyme into the non-native compartment__.

6. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the BMC polypeptide comprises a Eut polypeptide __and at least one additional BMC polypeptide from a different operon__.

7. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 6 wherein the Eut polypeptide comprises a EutS polypeptide __and the at least one additional BMC polypeptide comprises a shell protein__.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides __that are encoded by heterologous nucleic acid__.

9. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides __encoded by nucleic acid from different bacterial species__.

10. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides __encoded by nucleic acid from different BMC operons__.

11. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein at least one BMC polypeptide comprises an affinity tag __for purification of the non-native compartment__.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide, __wherein the non-native compartment is not naturally occurring in the host cell__.

13. (Original) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a bacterium.

14. (Original) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Enterobacteriaceae.

15. (Original) The method of claim 14 wherein the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae comprises E. coli.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Shewanellaceae __and the polynucleotide encodes BMC polypeptides from a different bacterial species__.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a yeast __and the polynucleotide encodes BMC polypeptides from a bacterial source__.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17 wherein the yeast comprises a member of the family Saccharomycetaceae __and the non-native compartment is not naturally occurring in yeast__.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 18 wherein the member of the family Saccharomycetaceae comprises Saccharomyces cerevisiae __and the BMC polypeptides are heterologous to the yeast__.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises an alga __and the polynucleotide encodes BMC polypeptides from a bacterial source__.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, and at least one enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product __within the non-native compartment, wherein the non-native compartment is not naturally occurring in the cell__.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a bioactive product __not naturally produced by the cell__.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a drug or a drug precursor __not naturally produced by the cell__.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biofuel or a precursor of biofuel production __not naturally produced by the cell__.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the at least one enzyme catalyzes a step in degrading or detoxifying a toxic substrate __within the non-native compartment__.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 further comprising isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments __from the cell__.

27. (Original) The method of claim 26 wherein at least a portion of the non-native compartment comprise an affinity tag and isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprises contacting a sample comprising the non-native compartments with an affinity substrate having selective affinity for the affinity tag.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments __wherein each compartment comprises the proteinaceous shell comprising at least one BMC polypeptide__.
